acceptanceCriteria.text: Sign-in accepts email + password with show/hide, validation, friendly errors, and preserves a sanitized next return path. Verified by replaying real form posts: wrong password and empty password render their messages, correct credentials return 303, and a hostile next value is discarded.

Sign-up collects full name, email, password, confirmation, and terms, and shows the email-verification state when confirmation is required. Field validation, the verification panel, and enumeration safety for an already-registered address are verified; creating a brand-new auth.users row through the form was not directly observed (no deliverable test address; hosted SMTP allows 2 emails/hour). See ticket Notes.

Forgot password sends a reset email using the configured production/local redirect URL and shows an enumeration-safe success state. An address with no account renders the same panel as one with an account.

Reset password validates the recovery session, updates the password, and routes onward; sign-out clears the session and returns to sign-in. Verified with a real recovery token: confirm 307, reset 303, rotated password accepted, old password rejected, sign-out 303.

After authentication the user profile is resolved server-side: no organization sends the user to organization setup, otherwise to next or /properties. Verified 303 to /onboarding/organization with no membership and 303 to /properties with one.

Organization setup creates the organization, an owner membership, and sets the active organization, without invitations or org switching. Verified against the hosted database: role=owner, status=active, active_organization_id set; taken/empty slug and short name each report on the correct field.

Security posture is preserved: verified server-side auth, no trusted client user ids, sanitized return paths, no service-role key exposure, no weakened middleware. The organization RPC returns unauthenticated to an anonymous caller; return-path validation now rejects every /auth/* path.
Validation suite passes (test, lint, typecheck, format:check, build, dashboard:update, dashboard:check, dashboard:health) and flows are verified against a running server.

title: Secure parcel ingestion RPCs
description: Restrict upsert_parcel_from_provider and upsert_parcel_zoning_from_provider to the Supabase service_role. Both are SECURITY DEFINER and bypass RLS, but a configuration audit found anon and authenticated still hold EXECUTE on the hosted project, so any holder of the publishable key can write shared parcel and zoning reference data. No application or UI behavior changes.

dependencies.note: Completed — created upsert_parcel_from_provider.
Completed — created upsert_parcel_zoning_from_provider.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Both ingestion RPCs explicitly REVOKE EXECUTE from public, anon, and authenticated, and GRANT EXECUTE only to service_role. Applied per-overload via a pg_proc loop in migration 20260804180000, which self-verifies with has_function_privilege and raises if any untrusted role retains access.

The hosted project reflects the corrected privileges; has_function_privilege reports false for anon and authenticated on both functions, and live calls return SQLSTATE 42501 permission denied for an anonymous caller and for a real signed-in user token.

Parcel import through the server-side service-role client still succeeds: a live Regrid parcel imported with geometry via the real importParcel path, and a repeat import reused the same row rather than duplicating it. The verification row was deleted afterward.

An automated regression test fails if a future migration reintroduces anon/authenticated execute access to an ingestion RPC — proven by temporarily reintroducing the original grant and observing the failure. It also carries an opt-in live probe (FORMETRIX_LIVE_RPC_CHECK=1), skipped by default so the suite stays offline.
No application code, UI, or unrelated migration was changed; test, lint, typecheck, format:check, build, dashboard:update, dashboard:check, and dashboard:health all pass.
